video_title: Debating if Klay Thompson could of EVER been a NUMBER 1 and does he even HELP Miami 👀

quotes.speaker: Theo Pinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Theo Pinson on Klay Thompson's physical decline and injury recovery
quotes.excerpt: He has almost like a peg leg and it's significantly smaller than his other leg.
quotes.quote: With Klay, just watching him the last two years here in Dallas, it seems like he's fell off a lot, significantly. I've watched him miss a lot of open shots, which he's never done. But then I was also able to watch him physically and look at his body and seeing that he didn't recover from his injury. He has almost like a peg leg and it's significantly smaller than his other leg. So with that being said, I just don't see, I don't know how much they can get from him at this point in his career.

quotes.speaker: Raymond Felton
quotes.summary_phrase: Raymond Felton on Klay Thompson's role and defensive decline
quotes.excerpt: He's not 3-and-D Klay anymore, but I think he can still be somewhat of three.
quotes.quote: I think it's predicated on what they're asking him to do. He's not 3-and-D Klay anymore, but I think he can still be somewhat of three. Now the defense aspect of it, yeah, I think he's not the best defensively as he used to be and everything else. But that often comes as you get older and you play in the league, that just happens. But with that being said, I think from a three standpoint with the guys that he has that commands so much attention, those threes are not as contested as they was in Dallas.

quotes.speaker: Charlie Villanueva
quotes.summary_phrase: Charlie Villanueva and Theo Pinson on Miami's need for a playmaker
quotes.excerpt: I still think they're missing that one playmaker that can go get them a bucket.

text_blocks.speaker: Charlie Villanueva
text_blocks.text: They may bring him off the bench though. They may start Tim Hardaway.

text_blocks.speaker: Theo Pinson
text_blocks.text: I think just for defensive purposes, you got to start Klay. If you're going to start Damian Lillard and Andrew Wiggins, you're fine. The thing is with this team, Klay doesn't have to be the old Klay defensively because they're already elite defensively. No one's questioning this team defensively. That is not a worry at all. My worry with this team is if Giannis is not making the play, who's making the play? You can play through Bam, but when Bam was great, he was a long big man and he had a bunch of snipers around him where he can be the Draymond Green where he's doing the short rolls, he's the one making the play at the top of the key. He had that camaraderie with Duncan Robinson and Tyler Herro and even Max Strus where it was this handoff for open threes and stuff like that. So Tim's definitely capable of that. I think Tim's going to have a really good year, but I still think they're missing that one playmaker that can go get them a bucket in the crunch time.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Draymond Green criticizes media narratives about Klay Thompson
quotes.excerpt: Let's stop acting like 2017 is Klay is going to Miami.
quotes.quote: I don't like how everybody is trying to act like, oh man, it's Klay Thompson, like Klay to the Heat. Like this is Klay of 2018. And the reason I don't like it is because I feel like everybody's trying to set Klay up for failure. And so I want to say it right here right now. Let's stop acting like 2017 is Klay is going to Miami. I wish sports media would speak to it more like when Ray Allen went to Miami. Like that's the role I'd expect of Klay. Don't try to set my brother up like you about to get the 2017 Klay so the moment you don't y'all can bash him. That's bullshit. He's going to year 16 of his career. We obviously know the injuries that he's faced. Yes, he is going to go provide shooting because he shoots the lights out the ball and when he's 60, he'll be able to shoot the lights out the ball.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Draymond Green on Klay Thompson's potential as a number one option
quotes.excerpt: There was a 90% chance my brother was going to leave Golden State and go elsewhere.
quotes.quote: Highly likely that after the 2019 playoffs, Klay Thompson was going to leave the Golden State Warriors and go be a number one option somewhere. Highly fucking likely. Then he got hurt and so he stayed. But one thing I can assure you, there was a 90% chance my brother was going to leave Golden State and go elsewhere and test that number one option thing out. Unfortunately, it wasn't in the cards for him and he got hurt and he never got the opportunity to. So now in turn, everyone wants to talk like, oh you couldn't do it like he wasn't going to. But I study the history. I do the research and I am going to appreciate and watch and know the Klay Thompson of 2017, 18, 19, he was capable. He just never got the opportunity to do the contractual obligations and once he fulfilled his contractual obligation, he then faced an ACL and Achilles in back-to-back years and missed two and a half years of basketball.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Draymond Green compares Klay Thompson to Reggie Miller
quotes.excerpt: Reggie Miller was a very, very, very extremely successful basketball player. He was a number one option.
quotes.quote: The funny part about saying Klay Thompson couldn't be a number one option is this: Reggie Miller was a number one option. Reggie Miller was a very, very, very extremely successful basketball player. He was a number one option. So you mean to tell me if Klay Thompson left the Golden State Warriors, he couldn't be a number one option, but Reggie Miller could? Blasphemous. But again, very easy to look at what happened from 2019 after injury to 2026 and say, no, no, no. But let's go before that.
